cards.subject: The Dominus vobiscum at a Sunday Mass, seen from inside the sanctuary, from just behind the priest. In the foreground, the priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, stands on the foot-pace of the high altar seen from behind, having turned from the altar toward the people, his hands extended toward them. Beyond him, beyond the altar rail, the whole congregation in the wooden pews of a tall stone nave, small, facing him: families, the women in veils and mantillas, an old man leaning on a cane, children, a nun in a grey habit. Two servers in cassock and surplice kneel on the lowest altar step at either side with their hands joined. Morning light falls from the high windows across the nave; far away at the back, the open west doors and the organ gallery with the schola. Warm, welcoming, solemn. Keep everything inside the pointed arch.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: After the Sign of the Cross, all standing, the priest at the chair, 'facing the people and extending his hands', greets them (GIRM 124; the Order of Mass: 'abrindo os braços, saúda o povo'). The chair faces the people at the head of the sanctuary (GIRM 310), so the card looks over the priest's shoulder at the assembly the Greeting makes manifest (GIRM 50).

sources.title: GIRM ch. 4, nos. 124 (the Greeting at the chair, facing the people, hands extended)

cards.subject: The Confiteor at the foot of the altar at a Sunday Mass, seen close from a side aisle of a stone church. In the foreground, half-length and in profile, three of the faithful kneel in a wooden pew with their heads bowed, each striking the breast with a closed right hand: a grey-haired man in a dark coat, a young woman in a white lace veil, and a small boy copying his father. Behind them more people kneel with bowed heads. Beyond the altar rail, far off and small, the priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, stands at the foot of the altar steps, bowing profoundly toward the altar with his hands joined; the server kneels on the step behind him and a little to his left. Above them rises a high altar with gradines: two of the six candles lit on the gradine, a central crucifix, three altar cards, and the tabernacle veiled in white silk; a white frontal. Subdued grey light, a contrite hush. Keep everything inside the pointed arch.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: The Confiteor, which all say together after a pause for silence, 'striking their breast' at the words of the excerpt (order-of-mass.json, order.penitential-act, Form A); all still standing, as from the Entrance to the end of the Collect (GIRM 43, 51).

cards.subject: The Kyrie at a sung Mass, seen from the organ loft at the back of a tall stone church, looking down the whole length of the nave. In the foreground, seen from behind, a schola of men and boys in cassocks and white surplices chants from the chant books held in their hands, beside the gilded pipes of the organ, where the organist sits at the keys. Below, the congregation in the pews, small, turned toward the altar. Far away at the head of the nave, beyond the altar rail, the priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, stands at the high altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, his hands joined; two servers kneel on the steps; a high altar with gradines: six tall candles lit on the gradine, a central crucifix, three altar cards, and the tabernacle veiled in white silk; a white frontal. Sunlight slants through the high windows. Prayerful, imploring, luminous. Keep everything inside the pointed arch.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: The Kyrie 'is usually executed by everyone, that is to say, with the people and the choir or cantor taking part in it' (GIRM 52), all standing (GIRM 43); so the card looks from the choir over the standing people to the priest at the chair.

sources.title: GIRM ch. 2, nos. 43, 52 (standing; the Kyrie, sung by the people with choir or cantor)

cards.excerptSource: content/of/order/order-of-mass.json order.gloria (first two lines, joined; verbatim in both languages)
cards.subject: The Gloria on a great feast, seen from low in the nave looking up. In the foreground, half-length, the congregation stands with faces lifted as the schola in the gallery sings: a mother in a lace mantilla, a father holding a small daughter, an old man with his hand missal open. The whole church blazes with light: beyond the altar rail, a high altar with gradines: six tall candles lit on the gradine, a central crucifix, three altar cards, and the tabernacle veiled in white silk; a white frontal, white lilies and roses on the gradine; the priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, stands small at the middle of the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, his hands extended and raised to the height of his shoulders as he intones. High overhead, filling the top of the arch, the painted vault of the church shows a fresco of angels in white and gold singing in a starry sky above shepherds and their sheep on a dark hillside. Jubilant, radiant, festive. Keep everything inside the pointed arch.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: The Gloria is sung by all standing on Sundays outside Advent and Lent and on solemnities and feasts (GIRM 43, 53, 126), so the card is a feast: six candles (GIRM 117), flowers around the altar rather than on it (GIRM 305). Its opening words are the angels' song at Bethlehem (Luke 2:14), painted as a fresco in the church's vault rather than as a vision.

sources.title: GIRM ch. 2, nos. 43, 53 (standing; the Gloria and when it is said)
GIRM ch. 4, nos. 117, 126 (candles; the Gloria)

cards.excerptSource: content/of/formularies/tempore/ordinary-time/week-2/sunday.json collect (its Trinitarian conclusion, line breaks joined, verbatim in both languages)
cards.subject: The Collect at a Sunday Mass, seen close and in profile. The priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, stands at the epistle corner of the high altar, facing the large red-bound Missal that rests on its bookstand on the altar, his hands extended before his breast, palms facing, no higher than his shoulders, his eyes on the open book; its gilt-edged pages show no letters and a ribbon marker hangs down. Beside the Missal, the epistle-side altar card, its print too small to read. Behind him, soft and indistinct, the gradine with its tall lit candles and the veiled tabernacle; a server in cassock and surplice kneels on the lowest step. Warm candlelight, stillness, gathered prayer. Keep everything inside the pointed arch.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: After 'Let us pray' and a brief silence, the priest says the Collect 'with hands extended' (GIRM 127), at the chair, with all standing (GIRM 43); the Missal is kept next to the chair (GIRM 118a) and the acolyte presents the book to the priest there (GIRM 189). The excerpt is the Trinitarian conclusion GIRM 54 gives for a Collect addressed to the Father.

sources.title: GIRM ch. 2, nos. 43, 54 (standing; the Collect and its conclusion)
GIRM ch. 4, nos. 118, 127, 189 (the Missal by the chair; the Collect with hands extended; the acolyte presents the book)

cards.subject: The Epistle at a sung Mass, seen from a side aisle. At the epistle side of the sanctuary, a young cleric, a lector in black cassock and white lace surplice, stands at a lectern draped in white silk, facing the altar, and chants from the large open book of lessons, one hand steadying the page; the pages show no letters. The congregation sits in the wooden pews beyond the altar rail and listens, half-length and in profile: a farmer with his cap in his lap, an old woman in a black veil with her hands folded, a girl in a white veil looking up at the lector. Beyond him, the priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, stands at the epistle corner of the high altar, reading the same Epistle in a low voice from the Missal; a high altar with gradines: six tall candles lit on the gradine, a central crucifix, three altar cards, and the tabernacle veiled in white silk; a white frontal. Clear daylight falls across the lectern. Attentive, calm. Keep everything inside the pointed arch.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: After the Collect all sit; the reader goes to the ambo and proclaims the First Reading from the Lectionary already placed there, 'to which all listen', and ends with the acclamation the people answer (GIRM 128, 43, 58–59). The reader is a layman in an alb, the attire GIRM 194 allows; the priest sits at the chair.

cards.subject: The Gradual at a Sunday sung Mass, seen from among the people. In the foreground, half-length and seen from behind and in profile, the congregation sits in the wooden pews and listens: a father with a small son on his knee, two elderly sisters in black lace veils sharing one hand missal, a young man with his hands clasped. Ahead, in the choir between the nave and the sanctuary, a schola of men in cassock and white surplice stands around a tall wooden lectern bearing a large open chant book, and chants the verses of the psalm, seen in profile, their faces lifted in song; the pages show only square neumes, no letters. Beyond them and the altar rail, the priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, stands at the epistle corner of the high altar, reading the Gradual in a low voice. Soft golden light, a gentle, meditative calm. Keep everything inside the pointed arch.

cards.subject: The Epistle at a Solemn High Mass, seen from low at the side of the sanctuary, looking up. The subdeacon, in a white tunicle over a lace alb with the maniple on his left arm, stands on the floor of the sanctuary at the epistle side, behind the celebrant, facing the altar, seen in profile, and chants the Epistle from the book of lessons held open in his hands; the pages show no letters. Above him, at the epistle corner of the high altar, the priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, reads the Epistle in a low voice, the deacon in a white dalmatic at his right; beyond, the gradine with its six tall lit candles, the crucifix and the tabernacle veiled in white. Behind and below, beyond the altar rail, the congregation sits in the pews listening, small; the long nave stretches back to a round rose window glowing high above the west doors. A shaft of sunlight falls across the subdeacon. Quiet, earnest. Keep everything inside the pointed arch.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: The Second Reading is proclaimed from the ambo by a reader, all seated and listening, with the same acclamation as the first (GIRM 130, 43); on Sundays it is from the Apostle, here Paul's First Letter to the Corinthians (Second Sunday, Year C), whence the carved St. Paul with his sword and book. The reader is a layman in ordinary dress, against the alb of the First Reading.

cards.excerptSource: content/of/formularies/tempore/ordinary-time/week-13/sunday.json readings.C.gospelAcclamation verse (whole, verbatim in both languages)
cards.subject: The Alleluia before the Gospel at a Solemn High Mass, seen from the side of the sanctuary. The deacon, in a white dalmatic over a lace alb, kneels on the edge of the foot-pace, bowed low, his hands joined, praying the Munda cor meum; on the altar before him lies the closed Book of the Gospels bound in red and gold. At the middle of the altar the priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, stands in profile having put incense into the thurible; behind the high altar rise the gradine, six tall lit candles, the crucifix and the tabernacle veiled in white. At the foot of the altar steps wait the subdeacon in a white tunicle, two acolytes in cassock and surplice holding tall lit candles, and a thurifer with a smoking thurible. In the foreground, in the choir stalls, a schola of men in cassock and surplice sings the Alleluia from a large chant book on a lectern. Expectant, joyful. Keep everything inside the pointed arch.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: The Alleluia is sung by everybody, standing, led by a cantor or choir (GIRM 62, 131); meanwhile the priest puts incense in the thurible and, 'with hands joined, bows profoundly before the altar' saying Munda cor meum, then takes up the Book of the Gospels from the altar, the candles and thurible going before him (GIRM 132–133).

sources.title: GIRM ch. 2, nos. 62 (the Acclamation before the Gospel)
GIRM ch. 4, nos. 131–133 (all rise; Munda cor meum; the Book of the Gospels taken from the altar)

cards.subject: The Gospel at a Solemn High Mass, seen from the nave looking up into the sanctuary at an angle. At the gospel side of the sanctuary, the deacon, in a white dalmatic over a lace alb, stands in profile and swings a smoking thurible toward the open Book of the Gospels, bound in red and gold, which the subdeacon in a white tunicle holds open before him with both hands; on either side of the subdeacon an acolyte in cassock and surplice holds a tall lit candle, facing the deacon, and the thurifer waits beside. At the epistle corner of the high altar the priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, stands turned toward the Gospel with his hands joined; the gradine with its six tall lit candles, the crucifix and the white-veiled tabernacle rise behind. In the foreground, beyond the altar rail, the congregation stands in the pews, half-length, everyone turned toward the Gospel, the women's heads covered. Clouds of incense rise through a shaft of sunlight. Reverent, majestic. Keep everything inside the pointed arch.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: The high point of the Liturgy of the Word (GIRM 60): at the ambo the priest announces the Gospel, the people acclaim 'Glory to you, O Lord', and he incenses the book, the ministers with candles and thurible having gone before him; all stand, turned toward the ambo (GIRM 133–134, 43). With no deacon, the priest proclaims it (GIRM 59).
